Maroun deposits \$500 000 into a retirement fund which earns compound interest at the rate of 0.3% per month.

parts.latex: Calculate the amount of money that Maroun withdrew at the end of the fifth month.

Maroun is going to withdraw \$7500 at the end of each month, starting from the end of the sixth month.

The recurrence relation $A_n=A_{n-1}\times 1.003-7500$ models this situation, where $A_n$ is the balance in the retirement fund at the end of the $n$th month.

Determine the balance in Maroun's retirement fund at the end of the seventh month.

Maroun is offered an alternative retirement fund, where interest is paid at 3.2% per annum, compounded daily.

By calculating the effective annual rate of interest for both retirement funds, or otherwise, determine whether Maroun should remain with the current retirement fund or change to the alternative retirement fund.

solutions.latex:
Balance at the end of the fourth month:
$$496994.00+1490.98-3800=494684.98$$

$\therefore$ Balance at the end of the fourth month is $\$494\,684.98$.

Interest earned at the end of the fifth month:
$$494684.98\times 0.003=1484.05$$

$\therefore$ Interest earned at the end of the fifth month is $\$1484.05$.

Amount Maroun withdrew at the end of the fifth month:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Balance} &= P+I-M \\ M &= P+I-\text{Balance} \\ &= 494684.98+1484.05-491969.03 \\ &= 4200 \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Maroun withdrew $\$4200$ at the end of the fifth month.
criteria: Finds the interest earned at the end of the fifth month, or equivalent merit
Finds the balance at the end of the fourth month, or equivalent merit
Determines the balance at the end of the sixth month, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Effective annual rate of interest for the current retirement fund:
$$\begin{aligned} (1+0.003)^{12}-1 &= 0.036599\ldots \\ &\approx 3.66\%\text{ p.a.} \end{aligned}$$

Effective annual rate of interest for the alternative retirement fund:
$$\begin{aligned} \left(1+\dfrac{0.032}{365}\right)^{365}-1 &= 0.032516\ldots \\ &\approx 3.25\%\text{ p.a.} \end{aligned}$$

The effective annual rate of interest for the alternative retirement fund is less than Maroun's current retirement fund, hence Maroun should stay with his current retirement fund.

Alternatively, compare the future value (FV) of one dollar invested in both funds.

Current fund:
$$\text{FV}=(1+0.3\%)^{12}=\$1.03659998$$

Alternative fund:
$$\text{FV}=\left(1+\dfrac{3.2\%}{365}\right)^{365}=\$1.032516057$$

The FV of the alternative fund is less than the FV of the current fund, hence Maroun should stay with his current retirement fund.
criteria: Finds the effective annual rate of interest for one of the funds, or equivalent merit

489.stem: Jack intends to deposit \$80 into a savings account on the first day of each month for 24 months. The interest rate during this time is 6\% per annum, compounded monthly.

figures.cap: partial table of future value interest factors with entry A

parts.latex: Calculate how much money Jack will have in his account at the end of the 24 months.

A table of future value interest factors could have been used to calculate how much money Jack would have in his account at the end of the 24 months.

Part of the table is shown.

\exfigure{1628_q24_1}

What is the value of $A$ in the table? Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places.
parts.note: Annuity interest-factor table look-up: Standard (2024 Advanced annuities use the GP formula only) · Standard: MST-12-S2-03

solutions.latex:
The monthly rate is $\dfrac{6\%}{12}=0.5\%$, so each month the balance is multiplied by $1.005$.

The first deposit accrues interest for 24 months.

$\therefore$ Its future value is $80(1.005)^{24}$.

The next deposit accrues interest for 23 months, and so on, down to 1 month for the last deposit.

Summing the geometric series ($a=1.005$, $r=1.005$, 24 terms):
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 80(1.005)^{24}+80(1.005)^{23}+\cdots+80(1.005)^{1}\\ &= 80\left[(1.005)^1+(1.005)^2+\cdots+(1.005)^{24}\right]\\ &= 80\times(1.005)\left[\dfrac{(1.005)^{24}-1}{1.005-1}\right]\\ &= 2044.73\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ Jack will have $\$2044.73$.
criteria: Sets up an appropriate series, or equivalent merit
Finds a correct term in the series, or equivalent merit

The future value of an annuity of \$1 for 24 periods is $A$, so the future value of \$80 per period is $80A$.
$$\begin{aligned} 80A &= 2044.73\\ A &= \dfrac{2044.73}{80}\\ &= 25.559\end{aligned}$$

The 2023 balance grows for 12 months at $0.5\%$ per month, plus the new annuity ($n=12$, $r=0.5\%$):
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= FV_{\text{lump}}+FV_{\text{instal}} \\ &= P(1+r)^n+M\times\text{factor} \\ &= 1233.56(1+0.5\%)^{12}+200\times 12.3356 \\ &= 3776.763\ldots \\ &\approx 3776.76 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ Hannah has \$3776.76.

When Fred was born, his parents opened a new savings account and made a deposit of \$300. At the start of each subsequent six-month period, his parents make a deposit of \$300. The account earns an interest rate of 6% per annum, compounded half-yearly.

Let $A_n$ be the amount (in dollars) in the account at the end of $n^{th}$ half-year.

parts.latex: Show that the amount available for withdrawal at the end of the 18$^{\text{th}}$ year will be \$19552 to the nearest dollar. (Assume that no withdrawals are made from the fund during this time.)

solutions.latex:
$r=\dfrac{6\%}{2}=3\%$ per half-year.

Each deposit is made at the start of a half-year and earns interest for that half-year:
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=300(1.03)\\A_2&=(A_1+300)\times1.03\\&=(300\times1.03+300)\times1.03\\&=300\times1.03^2+300\times1.03\end{aligned}$$

Continuing the pattern, the bracket is a GP with $a=1.03$, $r=1.03$ and $n$ terms, summed with $S_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$:
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=300(1.03)\\A_2&=300\times1.03^2+300\times1.03\\&\;\;\vdots\\A_n&=300\times1.03^n+300\times1.03^{n-1}+\dots+300\times1.03\\&=300(1.03^n+1.03^{n-1}+\dots+1.03)\\&=300\times1.03\times\dfrac{1.03^n-1}{1.03-1}\\&=10300(1.03^n-1)\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes an expression for $A_n$, or uses the sum of a GP formula without establishing $A_n$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
$18$ years $=36$ half-years, so $n=36$:
$$\begin{aligned}A_{36}&=10300(1.03^{36}-1)\\&=\$19\,552\text{ (nearest dollar)}\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
Melinda wishes to withdraw \$8000 at the end of each year for a period of $n$ years. Show that an expression for the minimum value of $Q$ is

$$\dfrac{8000}{1.035}+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^2}+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^3}+\cdots+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^n}$$
Hence, or otherwise, find the minimum value $Q$ that would permit Melinda to withdraw annual amounts of \$8000 indefinitely. Give your answer to the nearest dollar.

solutions.latex:
Let $A_n$ be the balance after the $n$th withdrawal. Each year the balance is multiplied by $1.035$, then $\$8000$ is withdrawn:
$$\begin{aligned} A_1&=Q\times1.035-8000 \\ A_2&=A_1\times1.035-8000 \\ &=\left(Q\times1.035-8000\right)1.035-8000 \\ &=Q\times1.035^2-8000\times1.035-8000 \\ A_3&=A_2\times1.035-8000 \\ &=Q\times1.035^3-8000\times1.035^2-8000\times1.035-8000 \\ &=Q\times1.035^3-8000\left(1.035^2+1.035+1\right) \end{aligned}$$
Continuing the pattern,
$$A_n=Q\times1.035^n-8000\left(1+1.035+\cdots+1.035^{n-1}\right)$$
The minimum value of $Q$ leaves nothing after $n$ withdrawals, $A_n=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} Q\times1.035^n&=8000\left(1+1.035+1.035^2+1.035^3+\cdots+1.035^{n-1}\right) \\ Q&=\dfrac{8000}{1.035^n}+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^{n-1}}+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^{n-2}}+\cdots+\dfrac{8000}{1.035} \\ &=\dfrac{8000}{1.035}+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^2}+\cdots+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^n} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the correct expression for $A_n$, or equivalent merit
Writes the correct expression for $A_1$, $A_2$ or $A_3$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The expression in part (a) is a geometric series with
$$\begin{aligned} a&=\dfrac{8000}{1.035} \\ r&=\dfrac{1}{1.035} \end{aligned}$$
Withdrawing indefinitely means $n\to\infty$, so the minimum value is the limiting sum (as $|r|<1$):
$$\begin{aligned} Q&=\dfrac{a}{1-r} \\ &=\dfrac{\frac{8000}{1.035}}{1-\frac{1}{1.035}} \\ &=\$228\,571.43 \\ &\approx\$228\,571 \text{ (nearest dollar)} \end{aligned}$$
Alternative solution: the yearly interest must cover the withdrawal, so
$$\begin{aligned} Q\times3.5\%&=8000 \\ Q&=\dfrac{8000}{3.5\%} \\ &=\$228\,571.43 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Uses the correct limiting sum expression to find the minimum value, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: An investment of \$4000 earns interest at a rate of $r\%$ p.a. over a period of one year. How much more interest would the investment earn, if interest is compounded half-yearly rather than yearly? Find the answer in terms of $r$.

solutions.latex:
With yearly compounding at $\dfrac{r}{100}$:
$$A_1=4000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{100}\right)$$
With half-yearly compounding the rate per half-year is $\dfrac{r}{200}$, for $2$ periods:
$$\begin{aligned} A_2 &= 4000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{200}\right)^2 \\ &= 4000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{100}+\dfrac{r^2}{40000}\right) \end{aligned}$$
The extra interest is
$$\begin{aligned} A_2-A_1 &= 4000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{100}+\dfrac{r^2}{40000}\right)-4000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{100}\right) \\ &= 4000\cdot\dfrac{r^2}{40000} \\ &= \dfrac{r^2}{10} \end{aligned}$$

The monthly rate is $\dfrac{3.6\%}{12}=0.3\%=0.003$, so each month's balance is multiplied by $1.003$.

Each deposit of \$300 is made at the start of the month, so it earns interest for that month.
$$\begin{aligned} A_1 &= 300(1.003) \\ A_2 &= \big(A_1+300\big)(1.003) \\ &= 300(1.003^2+1.003) \\ A_3 &= \big(A_2+300\big)(1.003) \\ &= 300(1.003^3+1.003^2+1.003) \end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$A_n=300\left(1.003^n+1.003^{n-1}+\cdots+1.003\right)$$
This is a geometric series with first term $a=300(1.003)$, common ratio $r=1.003$ and $n$ terms.

Using $S_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$:
$$\begin{aligned} A_n &= \dfrac{300(1.003)\left(1.003^n-1\right)}{1.003-1} \\ &= \dfrac{300.9}{0.003}\left(1.003^n-1\right) \\ &= 100300\left(1.003^n-1\right) \end{aligned}$$

Difference:

This is a GP with $a = 1.065$, $r = 1.065$ and $n$ terms, so $S_n = \dfrac{a(r^n - 1)}{r - 1}$.

$$\text{Amount} = 2000\times\dfrac{1.065(1.065^n - 1)}{1.065 - 1} = \dfrac{2130}{0.065}\left(1.065^n - 1\right)$$

We need the amount to exceed \$100000.

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{2130}{0.065}\left(1.065^n - 1\right) &> 100000 \\ 1.065^n &> 4.0516 \\ n &> \dfrac{\log 4.0516}{\log 1.065} \\ n &> 22.2 \end{aligned}$$

$n$ is a whole number of years, so $n = 23$.

$$\therefore\ \text{the amount first exceeds \$100000 at the end of 23 years}$$
criteria: Identifies the sum of a GP correctly, or equivalent merit

3479.stem:
John wants to accrue an investment of \$500 000 for his retirement in 30 years. He proposes to make a payment at the beginning of each year for the next 30 years.

The interest rate is set at $5\%$ p.a. At the end of $n$ years after starting his payments, the amount in the fund is $A_n$.

parts.latex: Show that $A_{30}=M\times 21\times(1.05^{30}-1)$
Hence, calculate the annual payment $M$.
After 20 years, John is able to increase his payment to \$8000 per year. What will be the new value of his investment at the end of the 30-year period?

solutions.latex:
Interest is $5\%$ p.a., so each year the amount is multiplied by $R=1.05$. Payments are made at the start of each year.
$$\begin{aligned} A_1 &= M(1.05) \\ A_2 &= \left[M(1.05)+M\right](1.05) \\ &= M(1.05)^2+M(1.05) \\ A_3 &= \left[M(1.05)^2+M(1.05)+M\right](1.05) \\ &= M(1.05)^3+M(1.05)^2+M(1.05) \end{aligned}$$
Continuing the pattern,
$$A_{30}=M\left[1.05+1.05^2+1.05^3+\dots+1.05^{30}\right]$$
This is a geometric series with $a=1.05$, $r=1.05$ and $30$ terms. Using $S_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$:
$$\begin{aligned} A_{30} &= M\left\{1.05\cdot\dfrac{1.05^{30}-1}{1.05-1}\right\} \\ &= M\left(\dfrac{1.05}{0.05}\right)\left(1.05^{30}-1\right) \\ &= M\times 21\times\left(1.05^{30}-1\right) \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Obtains correct expressions for $A_1$, $A_2$ and $A_3$ and attempts to form an expression for $A_{30}$, or starts at a correct expression for $A_{30}$ and correctly simplifies, or equivalent merit
Obtains correct expressions for $A_1$ and $A_2$, or forms a correct expression for $A_{30}$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Set $A_{30}=500\,000$ in the result from part (a):
$$\begin{aligned} M &= \dfrac{500\,000}{21\left(1.05^{30}-1\right)} \\ &\approx \$7167.35 \end{aligned}$$

For a constant payment $M$, $A_n=M(21)\left(1.05^n-1\right)$.

After $20$ years, with $M=\$7167.35$:
$$\begin{aligned} A_{20} &= 7167.35(21)\left(1.05^{20}-1\right) \\ &\approx \$248\,845.03 \end{aligned}$$
This grows for a further $10$ years, using $A=PR^n$:
$$\begin{aligned} A_{10} &= 248\,845.03(1.05)^{10} \\ &\approx \$405\,342.33 \end{aligned}$$
The new payments of $M=\$8000$ for $10$ years give
$$\begin{aligned} A_{10} &= 8000(21)\left(1.05^{10}-1\right) \\ &\approx \$105\,654.30 \end{aligned}$$
Add the two amounts:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= \$405\,342.33+\$105\,654.30 \\ &= \$510\,996.63 \end{aligned}$$

3522.stem: John's grandfather wishes to leave him \$250,000 in his will. He proposes to make a payment to an insurance company at the beginning of each year up until his death. The interest rate is set at 7% p.a. At the end of $n$ years after starting his payments, the amount in the fund is $A_n$. Let his first payment be \$$R$.

parts.latex:

Show that $A_{30}=R\left[\dfrac{1.07^{31}-1}{0.07}\right]$.

Each year the fund grows by 7%, and a payment of $R$ is added at the start of the year.
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=1.07A_0=1.07R\\ A_2&=(A_1+R)\times1.07\\ &=1.07^2R+1.07R\end{aligned}$$

Continuing in the same way:
$$\begin{aligned}A_3&=(A_2+R)\times1.07\\ &=1.07^3R+1.07^2R+1.07R\\ &\ \vdots\\ A_{30}&=1.07^{30}R+\dots+1.07^2R+1.07R\end{aligned}$$
The payout happens immediately after the last payment, so one more $R$ is added:
$$\begin{aligned}A_{30}&=1.07^{30}R+\dots+1.07^2R+1.07R+R\\ &=R\left[1.07^{30}+\dots+1.07+1\right]\end{aligned}$$
This is a geometric series with $a=1$, $r=1.07$ and $31$ terms (powers $0$ to $30$), so
$$A_{30}=R\left[\dfrac{1.07^{31}-1}{0.07}\right]$$

solutions.latex:
The balance is to reduce to $\$400\,000$. The bracket is a GP with $a=1$, $r=1.003$ and $n$ terms, so its sum is $\dfrac{1.003^n-1}{0.003}$.
$$400000=700000(1.003)^n-4000\left(\dfrac{1.003^n-1}{0.003}\right)$$

Each year the balance grows by $1.04$ and then $M$ is withdrawn:
$$\begin{aligned} A_{20} &= \left[26000\left(1.04^{18}-1\right)(1.04)-M\right](1.04)-M \\ &= 26000\left(1.04^{18}-1\right)(1.04)^2-M(1+1.04) \end{aligned}$$
$$A_{21}=26000\left(1.04^{18}-1\right)(1.04)^3-M\left(1+1.04+1.04^2\right)$$
By the pattern, using the geometric series sum $\dfrac{1.04^4-1}{0.04}=25\left(1.04^4-1\right)$:

The account is empty when $A_{22}=0$:
$$M=\dfrac{26000\left(1.04^{18}-1\right)(1.04)^4}{25\left(1.04^4-1\right)}$$
$$\therefore\ M=\$7347.66$$

A university student plans to finish university in two years time. He wishes to travel overseas and thinks he will need $\$15000$. He decides to invest $\$M$ at the start of each month in an investment account earning $3\%$ per annum compounded monthly.

Let $A_n$ be the amount at the end of $n$ months.

parts.latex: Find $A_2$ in terms of $M$.
Find the amount he must invest each month to reach his target of $\$15000$. Give your answer to the nearest dollar.

solutions.latex:
Interest is $\dfrac{3\%}{12}=0.25\%$ per month, so each amount is multiplied by $1.0025$ each month.

$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=M(1.0025)\\A_2&=\left[M(1.0025)+M\right](1.0025)\\&=M(1.0025)^2+M(1.0025)\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}A_3&=\left[M(1.0025)^2+M(1.0025)+M\right](1.0025)\\&=M(1.0025)+M(1.0025)^2+M(1.0025)^3\end{aligned}$$

So $A_n$ is a geometric series with first term $M(1.0025)$, ratio $1.0025$ and $n$ terms.

$$\begin{aligned}A_n&=M(1.0025)+M(1.0025)^2+\cdots+M(1.0025)^n\\&=M\left(\dfrac{1.0025(1.0025^n-1)}{1.0025-1}\right)\\&=401M(1.0025^n-1)\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Obtains the correct expression for $A_3$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Two years is $n=24$ months, with $A_{24}=15000$.

$$\begin{aligned}15000&=401M(1.0025^{24}-1)\\M&=605.703\ldots\end{aligned}$$

Therefore he must invest $\$606$ per month.

parts.latex: State the values of $P$ and $R$.

$B$ is the balance after one quarter: add interest of $\$9000$, then subtract the payment.

$$\begin{aligned}B&=750\,000+9000-17\,800\\&=741\,200\end{aligned}$$

$A$ is the interest on $B$ at $0.012$ per quarter.

$$\begin{aligned}A&=741\,200\times0.012\\&=\$8894.40\end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
Build the pattern from the recurrence $A_n=1.012A_{n-1}-17\,800$.

$$\begin{aligned}A_0&=750\,000\\ A_1&=1.012\times750\,000-17\,800\\ A_2&=1.012^2\times750\,000-17\,800(1.012+1)\\ A_3&=1.012^3\times750\,000-17\,800\left(1.012^2+1.012+1\right)\\ &\ \vdots\\ A_n&=1.012^n\times750\,000-17\,800\left(1.012^{n-1}+\dots+1\right)\end{aligned}$$

The bracket is a geometric series, so the account is empty when $A_n=0$:

$$0=1.012^n\times750\,000-17\,800\left(\dfrac{1.012^n-1}{0.012}\right)$$

Solving for $1.012^n$:

$$1.012^n=\dfrac{17\,800}{8800}$$

Taking logs to base $1.012$:

$$n=\log_{1.012}\left(\dfrac{17\,800}{8800}\right)=59.05541777\ldots$$

So there are $59$ full quarterly payments, and about $\$990$ is left for a smaller 60th payment.

$$\therefore\ 60 \text{ quarters}=15 \text{ years (the last payment is partial; } 59 \text{ full payments is about } 14.75 \text{ years)}$$

4860.stem:
On the 1st January 2021, Amanda invested \$7000 into a bank account that paid interest at a rate of 6% p.a. compounded annually. Amanda decided to add \$700 to her account on the 1st January each year, beginning in 2022.

Let $A_n$ be the amount in the account on the 1st January after $n$ years, after interest and her deposit has been paid.

parts.latex: Show that $A_2 = A_1 \times 1.06 + 700$.
Hence, determine how much was in her account on 1st January 2031, after interest and her deposit has been paid. Give your answer to the nearest dollar.

Amanda's friend, Bard, invested \$7000 into an account in a different bank on the 1st January 2021 and made no further payments. On 1st January 2031, Bard's balance was \$23\,417.

Calculate the annual rate of compound interest paid on Bard's account. Give your answer to 4 significant figures.

solutions.latex:
$A_1$ is the opening amount after one year's interest and the deposit.
$$A_1 = 7000 \times 1.06 + 700$$
In the second year the balance earns $6\%$ interest and then $\$700$ is added.
$$\begin{aligned} A_2 &= A_1 + 0.06A_1 + 700 \\ &= A_1 \times 1.06 + 700 \end{aligned}$$
Expanding,
$$\begin{aligned} A_2 &= (7000 \times 1.06 + 700) \times 1.06 + 700 \\ &= 7000 \times 1.06^2 + 700 \times 1.06 + 700 \end{aligned}$$

Continuing the pattern,
$$A_3 = 7000 \times 1.06^3 + 700 \times 1.06^2 + 700 \times 1.06 + 700$$
$$A_n = 7000 \times 1.06^n + 700 \times 1.06^{n-1} + \cdots + 700 \times 1.06 + 700$$
The terms after the first form a geometric series with $a = 700$, $r = 1.06$ and $n$ terms.
$$A_n = 7000 \times 1.06^n + \dfrac{700(1.06^n - 1)}{0.06}$$
1st January 2031 is $10$ years after 2021, so $n = 10$.
$$\begin{aligned} A_{10} &= 7000 \times 1.06^{10} + \dfrac{700(1.06^{10} - 1)}{0.06} \\ &\approx \$21\,762 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Identifies the pattern and the geometric series, or equivalent merit
Writes $A_3$ or the general pattern, or equivalent merit

$$\begin{aligned} 1 + \dfrac{R}{100} &= \sqrt[10]{\dfrac{23\,417}{7000}} \\ \dfrac{R}{100} &= \sqrt[10]{\dfrac{23\,417}{7000}} - 1 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ R \approx 12.83\%$$

5671.stem: Sam invests \$$M$ into an account at the beginning of each month. The account earns 3% p.a. interest, compounded monthly.

After the first five months of contributions, Sam increases his monthly payment to \$600. Given Sam's final contribution is less than \$600, what will be the minimum amount of this contribution (to the nearest \$5) to reach his goal of \$6000?

Interest per month is $\dfrac{3}{12}\%=0.25\%$, so each month the amount grows by a factor of $1.0025$.
$$A_1=M\times\left(1+\dfrac{3}{1200}\right)=M\times 1.0025$$
At the end of month 2, $A_1$ has grown once more and the second payment has grown for one month:
$$\begin{aligned} A_2&=A_1\times 1.0025+M\times 1.0025 \\ &=M\times 1.0025^2+M\times 1.0025 \\ &=M\left(1.0025+1.0025^2\right) \end{aligned}$$

Each payment earns interest for the months remaining, so
$$A_n=M\left(1.0025+1.0025^2+\dots+1.0025^n\right)$$
Factor out $1.0025$ to leave a geometric series with first term $1$, ratio $1.0025$ and $n$ terms:
$$A_n=M\times 1.0025\left(1+1.0025+\dots+1.0025^{n-1}\right)$$
Using $S_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$:
$$\begin{aligned} A_n&=M\times 1.0025\left(\dfrac{1.0025^n-1}{1.0025-1}\right) \\ &=401M\left(1.0025^n-1\right) \end{aligned}$$

5818.stem:
Janice deposits \$5000 into her savings account every year on January 1. During the year, the account receives compound interest of $6\%$ per annum, where interest is added to her account at the end of each year.

Let $J_n$ be the value of Janice's account immediately after her $n$th investment.

parts.latex:
Show that

$$J_n=\dfrac{250\,000\left(1.06^n-1\right)}{3}$$
Determine the minimum number of years until Janice's account contains \$100\,000.

solutions.latex:
Let $M=5000$ be the annual deposit. Each earlier deposit is multiplied by $1.06$ for each further year.
$$\begin{aligned} J_2&=1.06M+M\\ J_3&=(1.06M+M)\times1.06+M\\ &=M+1.06M+1.06^2M\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$J_n=M+1.06M+1.06^2M+\dots+1.06^{n-1}M$$
This is a geometric series with $n$ terms, first term $M$ and $r=1.06$.
$$\begin{aligned} J_n&=\dfrac{M\left(1.06^n-1\right)}{1.06-1}\\ &=\dfrac{5000\left(1.06^n-1\right)}{0.06}\\ &=\dfrac{250\,000\left(1.06^n-1\right)}{3}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes the series for $J_n$ (following from the working), or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Solve $J_n=100\,000$.
$$\begin{aligned} 100\,000&=\dfrac{250\,000\left(1.06^n-1\right)}{3}\\ \dfrac{30}{25}&=1.06^n-1\\ 1.06^n&=2.2\end{aligned}$$
Taking logarithms,
$$\begin{aligned} n&=\log_{1.06}2.2\\ &=\dfrac{\log2.2}{\log1.06}\\ &\approx13.5\end{aligned}$$
$n$ must be a whole number of instalments, so round up.

$$\therefore\ n=14,\ \text{on the payment of the 14th instalment, at the start of the 14th year}$$
